title: Absolute continuity via singletons
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite measurable space, and let $\mu$ and $
u$ be two measures on $\Omega$. Then $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$, written $\mu \ll 
u$, if and only if for every point $\omega \in \Omega$ with $
u(\{\omega\}) = 0$ one also has $\mu(\{\omega\}) = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: finite measurable space (finite type, every subset measurable)
two measures μ and ν on Ω
replaced:
On a finite measurable space, two measures satisfy $\mu \ll \nu$ if and only if for
every $\omega \in \Omega$, $\nu(\{\omega\}) = 0$ implies $\mu(\{\omega\}) = 0$.
